close_reason: Investigated: match_count pattern is correct per RFC 5280 §6.1.3(d)(1)(i). Multiple children with same valid_policy OID are the correct output when multiple parents match. Downstream code handles duplicates correctly via any()/contains(). Pre-existing, no bug.
description: pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2107-2122 (pre-existing, not introduced by today's commits) — match_count counts all parent nodes at depth cert_depth-1 whose expected_policy_set contains p_oid, then creates one new PolicyNode per parent count. RFC 5280 §6.1.3(d)(1)(i) says: for each matching parent, create one child with valid_policy = p_oid. With policy mappings, multiple parents can have the same p_oid in their expected_policy_set. This correctly creates multiple children, each representing a different inheritance path. However, all children have the same valid_policy = p_oid, creating duplicate OIDs at cert_depth in the flat tree. The §6.1.5(g) intersection logic and prune_policy_tree both iterate the tree by valid_policy and may over-count or behave incorrectly when the same policy OID appears multiple times at the same depth. Separately: for the typical case (zero or one parent), this is correct. The bug manifests only with policy-mapped certificates where multiple parents carry the same expected policy. Needs a PKITS policy-mapping test case to confirm.
notes: Investigation: The match_count pattern is correct per RFC 5280 §6.1.3(d)(1)(i) — one child per matching parent is the intended behavior. Duplicate valid_policy OIDs at the same depth are handled correctly by downstream code: prune_policy_tree uses any(), §6.1.5(g) uses contains() for dedup. This is pre-existing, not introduced today. Deferring; would need PKITS 4.12.x (policy mapping) suite to confirm. No code change needed.
title: policy tree §6.1.3(d)(1)(i) creates duplicate child nodes
